claims.claim: Kriss argues that in the AI dismissive formula an X with Y and Z, one or both attributes are either already implicit in X or make no sense at all.
claims.source: Sam Kriss, The New York Times Magazine, 2025
claims.page: section on the 'an X with Y and Z' tic

claims.feature: other: too much consistency or none
claims.claim: Kriss argues the model cannot get the balance right: either it imposes too much consistency, making its language redundant, or too little, turning it into drivel.
claims.source: Sam Kriss, The New York Times Magazine, 2025
claims.quote: it imposes too much consistency, in which case its language is redundant
claims.page: section on the 'an X with Y and Z' tic

claims.claim: Kriss attributes the failure to the models never having experienced the world, so everything they know reaches them through statistical correlations within quantities of words.
claims.source: Sam Kriss, The New York Times Magazine, 2025
claims.quote: Everything they know about the world comes to them through statistical correlations
claims.page: section citing Woolf's 'great plateful of blue water'

claims.claim: Kriss cites a generated phrase describing a studio that smelled of turpentine and dreams as a cheap literary effect that AI cannot avoid, since all it can do is pile concepts until they collapse.
claims.source: Sam Kriss quoting his own ChatGPT-5 output, The New York Times Magazine, 2025

claims.claim: Kriss reports that researchers found most people vastly prefer AI-generated poetry to the actual works of Shakespeare, T.S. Eliot and Emily Dickinson.
claims.source: Sam Kriss relaying a study, The New York Times Magazine, 2025
claims.quote: most people vastly prefer A.I.-generated poetry to the actual works of Shakespeare

claims.claim: Kriss characterises the resulting public voice as mixed metaphors and empty sincerity, impersonal and overwrought, and says it is how corporations and elected officials now speak.
claims.source: Sam Kriss, The New York Times Magazine, 2025
claims.quote: Mixed metaphors and empty sincerity. Impersonal and overwrought.
claims.page: section on the Starbucks closure notice

claims.claim: Kriss reports that British MPs began opening speeches with 'I rise to speak', an American convention, and that on a single day in June it happened 26 times.
claims.source: Sam Kriss, The New York Times Magazine, 2025
claims.quote: On a single day this June, it happened 26 times.

claims.claim: Kriss reports a Max Planck Institute for Human Development study that analysed more than 360,000 YouTube videos of extemporaneous academic talks and found AI language increasingly coming out of human mouths.
claims.source: Sam Kriss relaying a Max Planck study, The New York Times Magazine, 2025

claims.feature: other: what the machine says about itself is wrong
claims.claim: Kriss reports that ChatGPT describes its own prose as too clean and neutral, and asserts that this is not remotely true because the writing is not smooth or neutral but weird.
claims.source: Sam Kriss, The New York Times Magazine, 2025
claims.quote: It’s not smooth or neutral at all — it’s weird
claims.page: section beginning 'If we’re going to turn over essentially all communication'

claims.feature: other: parody passage in the AI voice
claims.claim: Kriss opens the essay with a paragraph written in the AI voice as a demonstration, whose clauses include the claim that the writing does not open up the tapestry of human experience.
claims.source: Sam Kriss, parody passage written by the author in the machine's voice, The New York Times Magazine, 2025
claims.quote: It doesn’t open up the tapestry of human experience

claims.claim: Taha Yasseri compared 1,800 matched article pairs and found Grokipedia averages about 14,200 words against 9,400 on Wikipedia.
claims.source: Taha Yasseri, Trinity College Dublin, arXiv:2510.26899v2
claims.quote: Grokipedia articles average about 14,200 words versus 9,400 on Wikipedia

claims.claim: Yasseri measured a mean Flesch-Kincaid grade of 19.3 for Grokipedia against 12.8 for Wikipedia across 1,811 matched pairs.
claims.source: Taha Yasseri, Trinity College Dublin, arXiv:2510.26899v2
claims.quote: indicating more syntactically complex and less reader-friendly prose

claims.claim: Yasseri measured 21.4 references per thousand words on Grokipedia against 90.2 on Wikipedia, and 2.87 headings per thousand words against 5.58.
claims.source: Taha Yasseri, Trinity College Dublin, arXiv:2510.26899v2
claims.quote: longer but less lexically diverse articles, with fewer references per word

claims.claim: Yasseri's measured lexical diversity gap is very small: type-token ratio 0.244 on Grokipedia against 0.248 on Wikipedia, a difference of 0.004 at p equals 0.02.
claims.source: Taha Yasseri, Trinity College Dublin, arXiv:2510.26899v2
claims.quote: inflates sentence length and readability grade without a proportional increase in lexical variety

claims.claim: Yasseri concludes that AI-generated encyclopedic content mirrors Wikipedia's informational scope but diverges in editorial norms, favouring narrative expansion over citation-based verification.
claims.source: Taha Yasseri, Trinity College Dublin, arXiv:2510.26899v2
claims.quote: favoring narrative expansion over citation-based verification
